newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish insurer Polisa sees mid-November listing.
newsitem.headline: Polish insurer Polisa sees mid-November listing.

text.p: The Polish insurance company TUR Polisa SA, the shares of which had been cleared for bourse trade on Wednesday, wants to enter the exchange's main market in mid-November, the president of the company said on Thursday.
"We would like to enter the bourse in mid-November," Stanislaw Gutek told Reuters in an interview.

He said that at the bourse's request the company was going to supply updated information on the company's dividend policy for the next few years and earnings forecast for 1996 and 1997 before the bourse debut.
Gutek said the firm also was going to deliver requested information on compatibility of its investment with the insurance law.

Polisa, Poland's third largest insurer whose public offering late in 1995 was undersubscribed, applied for bourse listing early this year but put off its bid to gain time to return to black after first quarter losses.

Gutek said the company saw up to 4.5 million zlotys of additional costs in the next four or five years because it would have to cover the costs of its "stop loss" reinsurance agreements used to cover large payouts at the start of 1996.
"It will potentially lower our profits but taking into account our expected growth it (the "stop loss" arrangement) will be better for the client than traditional reinsurance agreements," he said.
